title: The Rakish Viscount's Pretend Wife
subtitle: A Clean Regency Romance Novella
kicker: Fake marriage at a snowbound inn
meta: A clean Regency romance novella. A governess and a rakish viscount, snowed in at a coaching inn, pose as husband and wife. By Emma Velott.
short: Stranded at a snowbound inn, governess Delilah Pearce agrees to pose as Simon Cathcart's wife to protect her reputation. Their rules are quite clear. Their feelings prove less cooperative.
blurb: Six years of relentless propriety have kept Delilah Pearce employed, respectable, and entirely alone. Then a snowstorm strands her at a coaching inn, and she climbs the stairs to the room she paid for and finds a stranger sprawled across the mattress, one boot on, snoring like a man trying to expel his own soul.

Simon Cathcart has woken in a great many beds that were not his. This is the first one that arrives with a wife attached, since he apparently announced the imminent arrival of one before the brandy finished with him, and the innkeeper believed every word.

The storm will not lift for days, and a governess caught sharing a room with a rake has no career left to speak of. So Delilah sets her terms. He will play the adequate husband, keep to the left side of the bed, and keep his hands, his remarks, and his eyebrows entirely to himself.
The terms hold rather better than either of them expected. What refuses to hold is everything underneath them.
A clean, closed-door Regency novella about a fake marriage, a snowbound inn, and two people who agreed on the rules long before they understood the cost.

title: A Fiery Widow for the Cold Duke
subtitle: A Clean Regency Duke Romance
meta: A clean grumpy duke romance. A fiery widow becomes housekeeper to the cold Duke of Wrenwick, and an arrangement turns into marriage. By Emma Velott.
short: Widow Anastasia Reddington accepts a position at Wrenwick Hall and refuses to be intimidated by its cold duke. An unexpected marriage brings her closer to the man behind his carefully guarded silence.
hook: She has run out of patience. He has run out of excuses.
blurb: Fourteen months of widowhood have left Anastasia Reddington with two rented rooms, a ledger that refuses to balance, and a temper she has swallowed so often it sits in her like a coal that will not go out. When a position at Wrenwick Hall is offered at twice the going rate, she takes it, and she does not ask why nobody else would.
Alexander, Duke of Wrenwick, has emptied his own house. Servants flinch. Footmen leave. The table is laid every morning for a man who never eats at it. He expects the new housekeeper to last a week.
She lasts three days before telling him, to his face, that fear is the most expensive economy he has ever practised.

What begins as a trial becomes an arrangement, and the arrangement becomes a marriage neither of them planned to want. Then a charming young clergyman takes an interest in the new duchess, an old secret surfaces that someone has been saving for years, and Anastasia discovers how much of her husband's coldness was only ever armour.
A clean, closed-door Regency romance with a grumpy duke, a widow who has finally run out of saying nothing, and a hard-won happily ever after.

title: A Jilted Bride for the Battle-Scarred Duke
subtitle: A Clean Regency Duke Romance
meta: A clean scarred duke romance. A jilted vicar's daughter becomes companion at Penwythe, home of a reclusive, battle-scarred duke. By Emma Velott.
short: After a public jilting, Ariana Raye becomes companion to a duke's young sister. Her new employer, Ronan Kingsford, has retreated from the world. Ariana's refusal to overlook him begins a slow and unexpected connection.
hook: Jilted in a ballroom with three hundred people watching, and the first thing she feels is not heartbreak.
blurb: Ariana Raye is a vicar's daughter with her father's debts hanging round her neck, and when Lionel Lockhart withdraws from their engagement in the middle of a ball, what rises in her once the shock clears is a clean and unladylike fury. A ruined woman takes what work she can get, which is how she comes to be rattling toward Penwythe in a hired coach while the driver explains that nobody has been past those gates in four years.

Ronan Kingsford, sixth Duke of Penwythe, came back from the war with a hand that will not close, a face he refuses to look at, and four rules that keep him upright. Rise at five. Dress without help. Do not leave the east wing. Do not look in mirrors.
The rules were working perfectly well until a voice started carrying through the plaster.

Hired as companion to the duke's young sister, Ariana has no intention of being anybody's cure. She simply declines to pretend the man does not exist. What grows between them is slow, reluctant and thoroughly inconvenient, and it is very nearly enough, right until the man who jilted her walks back through the door with a use for her after all.
A clean, closed-door Regency romance with a scarred recluse, a heroine who refuses to be made small, and a happily ever after earned the hard way.

title: Twelve Days to Keep an Earl
subtitle: A Hollybourne Christmas Novella
kicker: Fake courtship in a snowbound village
meta: A clean Regency Christmas novella. A squire's plain-spoken daughter and a charming earl agree to a pretend courtship until Twelfth Night. By Emma Velott.
short: Goldie Peverell wants one Christmas without a suitor. Jules Everleigh, the new Earl of Wintermere, wants a village that will stop glaring at him. Twelve days of pretending ought to settle both.
hook: “I am afraid this tree is taken. There is a very roomy headstone to your left.”
blurb: Three London Seasons have taught Goldie Peverell exactly what gentlemen think of a squire's daughter with red hair, a hearty laugh and opinions. This Christmas her mother has produced a magistrate from York who admires her robust constitution, and Goldie escapes him by running into the churchyard and straight into the boy who left Hollybourne eight years ago.

Jules Everleigh has come home an earl, to a shuttered Hall, a broken mill wheel and a dale that remembers what his father did to it. He has a letter in his pocket that he shows to nobody, and he has until just after Twelfth Night to answer it.

So they strike a bargain under the yew tree. For twelve days he will pay her such marked attention that no other suitor dares approach, and she will walk him through every cottage door in the village until Hollybourne remembers how to like him.

It is a sensible arrangement between old friends. It survives a skating party, a great deal of bad poetry and a midnight knock at the door on New Year's Eve, and then it begins to feel alarmingly like the truth.
A light-hearted, clean and closed-door Regency Christmas novella with a pretend courtship, a managing heroine and an earl who has to earn his welcome.

title: Twelve Nights to Trust a Duke
subtitle: A Hollybourne Christmas Novella
kicker: A bluestocking, a stranger and a snowed-in library
meta: A clean Regency Christmas novella. A bluestocking cataloguing a duke's library finds a forgery and a scarred stranger who knows too much. By Emma Velott.
short: Harriet Lisle trusts nothing she cannot hold to the light. Snowed in at Thornleigh to catalogue a duke's library, she finds a forged book and a scarred stranger who already knows it is there.
hook: “Perhaps I am a very literate brute.” “Perhaps you are a very badly disguised one.”
blurb: Harriet Lisle earns her bread cataloguing other people's libraries, and five hard years have taught her to take nobody at his word. She arrives at Thornleigh on Christmas Eve, in a snowstorm, to list the Duke of Ravensmoor's books while his Grace is away in London.

Within two hours she has found a rare Sophocles that is a very beautiful fake. Within two hours and a minute, the terrace doors have burst open on a tall, unshaven man with a scar along his jaw, who calls himself Mr. Graves, claims to manage the estate, and recognizes the book from forty paces.

Somebody has been emptying the library a volume at a time. He cannot prove who. She can tell a forgery by its paper. So they make a bargain to work together by candlelight, twelve nights, with the snow piling against the windows and a great many arguments about evidence.
Harriet tests everything. She has tested Mr. Graves by every measure she owns, and he has passed them all, which is a pity, since there is one thing he has not told her.
A clean, closed-door Regency Christmas novella with a hidden identity, a snowbound mystery and a heroine who has to decide what a man's word is worth.

title: Twelve Days to Teach a Marquess
subtitle: A Hollybourne Christmas Novella
kicker: The governess and the charming marquess
meta: A clean Regency Christmas novella. A governess has twelve days to make London's most charming trifler fit to propose by Twelfth Night. By Emma Velott.
short: The Marquess of Stratton must be betrothed by Twelfth Night or lose a fortune. Governess Judith Carrow has twelve days to teach him how to be serious, and a firm rule against being charmed.
hook: “You will be betrothed by Twelfth Night, Felix, or I leave every farthing to Reginald.”
blurb: Felix Danvers, Marquess of Stratton, has been charming for ten years without once being serious, and his grandmother has had enough. On Christmas morning she gives him twelve days to become betrothed, and a governess to see that he manages it.

Miss Judith Carrow has polished seven years of awkward heiresses into brides. She owns a burgundy gown, a black cloth book and a perfectly sound rule about gentlemen who smile too easily. One idle marquess ought to be no trouble at all.

So the lessons begin. How to pay a compliment and mean it. How to dance a reel without mocking it. How to tell a lady the truth. He proves a maddeningly quick pupil, and he is hiding something behind a green baize door that explains a great deal about him.
Then the eligible young ladies arrive for the house party, and Judith discovers how little she enjoys her own success.
A light-hearted, clean and closed-door Regency Christmas novella with a governess, a wager on a staircase and a hero who has to learn to say what he means.
